items.content_html:
Fixes #33746 (parts 1, 2, 4, 6).

Corrections verified against the WAI-ARIA spec:

  1. Example context: replaced the dialog example with application (dialog is a window role per the spec, not a composite widget; document is only useful as a focusable accessibility child of a widget or application role).
  2. aria-expanded: removed from associated properties and Required JS features (document's Supported States and Properties list is empty in the spec).
  3. tabindex: clarified it is an HTML attribute, not an ARIA state/property.
  4. document/article relationships: clarified that document defines no relationship to other document elements, and article association is conveyed via context, not programmatically.
items.title: Correct document role page per ARIA spec

items.content_html:
Fixes #45101.

Per CSS Containment Level 2 (css-contain-2 §containment-paint), the contents of a paint-contained element are clipped to its overflow clip edge (taking corner clipping into account), not its border-box. The overflow clip edge defaults to the padding-box edge and can be extended via overflow-clip-margin (css-overflow-3).

Verified against the spec sources:

  • css-contain-2/Overview.bs: "must be clipped to the overflow clip edge of the paint containment box"
  • css-overflow-3/Overview.bs: overflow-clip-margin "If omitted, defaults to padding-box"
items.title: Describe contain: paint clipping to overflow clip edge

Description

Chrome 150 supports Processing Instructions in HTML documents.

Prior to this they were treated as comments by all browsers as noted in the current docs

Warning: ProcessingInstruction nodes are only supported in XML documents, not in HTML documents. In these, a process instruction will be considered as a comment and be represented as a Comment object in the tree.

This warning is now no longer accurate.

Chrome also added some extra methods (getAttribute, getAttributeNames...etc) similar to the equivalents on Element so this PR adds those docs (based on the Element versions).

Description

Improve the Web Audio API guide by adding guidance on creating and composing audio effects, including a concrete BiquadFilterNode example and a reference to the Voice-change-O-matic implementation.

Motivation

The existing guide explains basic audio graphs and modification nodes, but does not clearly explain how readers can create new audio effects by combining audio nodes. This change provides a practical pattern for adding effects and explains how the Voice-change-O-matic example uses single-node and multi-node effect graphs.

Additional details

The new section covers:

  • Connecting an effect node between an audio source and destination.
  • Combining multiple audio nodes to create more complex effects.
  • Creating a BiquadFilterNode and adding it to an audio graph.
  • How Voice-change-O-matic uses WaveShaperNode, BiquadFilterNode, ConvolverNode, DelayNode, and GainNode to implement different effects.
  • How to add and switch between effect graphs in an application.

items.content_html:
Summary

This PR clarifies the dispatch timing of the selectionchange event across Document, HTMLInputElement, and HTMLTextAreaElement documentation.

Per section 3.3 of the W3C Selection API specification, selectionchange is scheduled asynchronously as a task in the user interaction task queue rather than fired synchronously when the selection changes. This behavior differs from many other input/UI events and means listeners fire on the next turn of the event loop rather than within the same call stack.

Closes #45082

Changes Made

  • Document selectionchange event: Added an explanatory note in the Description section describing asynchronous task scheduling.
  • HTMLInputElement selectionchange event: Clarified that selection changes are dispatched asynchronously via the task queue.
  • HTMLTextAreaElement selectionchange event: Updated to maintain consistency across text control docs.

Verification

  • Ran Prettier formatting check across all modified pages.

Signed-off-by: Poorvith M P poorvith007@proton.me
items.title: docs(web-api): document asynchronous task queuing for selectionchange event

Description

Updated the example. The current example makes it look like the media query detects if an element is overflowing, not how the device handles overflow. I added a paragraph that isn't overflowing, and a note in the CSS to explain that it's about how the device handles overflow.

Motivation

There is a note at the top of the page that explains this, but with the example only showing it working on an overflowing paragraph, which I think a lot of people will skip to, and then assume it will detect overflows. Just wanted to help make it more clear that isn't how this works.

Description

Mention the unexpected font-family: monospace behavior and a workaround for it.

Motivation

This behavior is unintuitive and may confuse developers unfamiliar with it. For this reason I think that it is good to have a note explicitly mentioning it on the MDN page.

Additional details

I can't find this behavior in the spec itself, but there are many references to it online:

  • https://meyerweb.com/eric/thoughts/2010/02/12/fixed-monospace-sizing/
  • https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38781089/font-family-monospace-monospace

And you can try it out yourself:

<p style="font-family: monospace, monospace">Normal text</p>
<p style="font-family: monospace">Small text</p>
